title: Test chunked generation - refactor authentication system with RBAC, OAuth2, session management, and audit logging

userStories.title: Database schema for RBAC roles and permissions
userStories.description: Create PostgreSQL migrations for the RBAC system including roles, permissions, role_permissions, and user_roles tables. This forms the foundational data model for all authorization decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates roles table with id, name, description, is_system_role, created_at columns
Migration creates permissions table with id, name, resource, action, description columns
Migration creates role_permissions junction table with FK constraints to both tables
Migration creates user_roles junction table linking users to roles with FK constraints
Migration runs cleanly via pg-index.ts migration runner with timestamp prefix format
Unique constraints exist on roles.name and permissions.name columns

userStories.title: RBAC service layer for role and permission management
userStories.description: Implement a RbacService class in backend/src/lib/rbac.ts that provides CRUD operations for roles and permissions, plus methods to assign/revoke roles from users and check permissions.
acceptanceCriteria: RbacService.createRole(name, description) inserts into roles table and returns the created role
RbacService.assignPermissionToRole(roleId, permissionId) creates role_permissions record
RbacService.assignRoleToUser(userId, roleId) creates user_roles record
RbacService.hasPermission(userId, resource, action) returns boolean by joining user_roles → role_permissions → permissions
RbacService.getUserPermissions(userId) returns all effective permissions for a user
All methods use typed pg query helpers and throw AppError subclasses on invalid inputs

userStories.title: Seed default system roles and permissions
userStories.description: Create a seeding script that initializes the default system roles (admin, member, viewer) and the permission set covering all Rorca resources (specs, runs, workspaces, direction, settings). This runs as part of the migration pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: Seed creates admin role with all permissions across all resources
Seed creates member role with read/write permissions on specs and runs, read-only on direction
Seed creates viewer role with read-only permissions on specs, runs, and direction
Seed is idempotent — running twice does not create duplicate rows (uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
Permissions follow resource:action naming convention (e.g. specs:create, runs:trigger, settings:write)
Seed runs automatically after migrations in pg-index.ts startup sequence

userStories.title: requirePermission middleware for route-level authorization
userStories.description: Implement an Express middleware factory requirePermission(resource, action) that checks if the authenticated user has the required permission via RbacService. Integrates with the existing auth middleware chain.
acceptanceCriteria: requirePermission('specs', 'create') returns 403 ForbiddenError when user lacks the permission
requirePermission passes to next() when user has the required permission
Middleware reads userId from res.locals.userId (set by authRequired)
Permission check result is cached per-request in res.locals to avoid duplicate DB queries
Middleware works with the existing authRequired middleware (called after it in the chain)
Returns { error: 'Insufficient permissions', code: 'forbidden', details: { resource, action } } on 403

userStories.title: Role and permission management API endpoints
userStories.description: Add Express routes for managing roles and permissions via the REST API, including CRUD for roles, permission assignment, and user role management. Endpoints require admin permission.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/auth/roles returns paginated list of all roles with their permissions
POST /api/auth/roles creates a new role (requires settings:write permission)
PUT /api/auth/roles/:roleId/permissions assigns permissions to a role (requires settings:write)
POST /api/auth/users/:userId/roles assigns a role to a user (requires settings:write)
DELETE /api/auth/users/:userId/roles/:roleId revokes a role from a user (requires settings:write)
All endpoints have JSDoc @swagger annotations and validate input with Zod schemas

userStories.title: OAuth2 provider configuration schema and storage
userStories.description: Create the database schema and configuration layer for OAuth2 providers. Support GitHub (already partially implemented), Google, and generic OIDC providers. Store client credentials securely in the vault.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds oauth_providers table with id, provider_type, client_id, client_secret_vault_key, scopes, enabled, created_at columns
provider_type enum includes: github, google, oidc
OAuthProviderService.getEnabledProviders() returns configured providers without exposing client secrets
Client secrets are stored via existing vault_keys table (AES-256-GCM), not as plaintext
GET /api/auth/providers returns list of enabled providers with name, type, and authorization_url (no secrets)
Migration uses timestamp prefix format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS

userStories.title: Generic OAuth2 authorization code flow handler
userStories.description: Implement a reusable OAuth2 handler in backend/src/lib/oauth2.ts that handles the authorization URL generation, callback validation, and token exchange for any configured provider. Replaces the GitHub-specific implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: generateAuthUrl(provider, state) returns a properly constructed authorization URL with all required params
handleCallback(provider, code, state) exchanges the code for tokens and returns user profile data
State parameter is validated using a server-side nonce stored in a short-lived DB record to prevent CSRF
Token exchange uses node-fetch and handles provider-specific response formats
Profile normalization returns { providerId, email, name, avatarUrl } regardless of provider
Existing GitHub OAuth flow is refactored to use this generic handler without behavior change

userStories.title: OAuth2 user account linking and registration
userStories.description: Implement the user account creation and linking logic when a user authenticates via OAuth2. If the email matches an existing user, link the OAuth identity. If new, create the account. Handle conflicts gracefully.
acceptanceCriteria: oauth_identities table is created with user_id, provider, provider_user_id, email, linked_at columns
If OAuth email matches existing user, the identity is linked and user is logged in (no duplicate account)
If no matching user exists, a new user account is created with the OAuth provider's email and name
If provider_user_id already linked to a different account, returns 409 ConflictError
New OAuth-registered users receive the 'member' default role automatically
The callback endpoint issues JWT + refresh token pair upon successful OAuth authentication

userStories.title: JWT access token and refresh token implementation
userStories.description: Refactor the existing JWT implementation to use short-lived access tokens (15 min) with long-lived refresh tokens (7 days). Store refresh tokens in the database for revocation support.
acceptanceCriteria: Access tokens expire in 15 minutes (exp claim), refresh tokens expire in 7 days
refresh_tokens table stores hashed token, user_id, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at, user_agent
POST /api/auth/refresh validates the refresh token, issues new access+refresh pair (rotation), and revokes old token
Revoked or expired refresh tokens return 401 AuthError with code: token_expired
JWT payload includes userId, email, plan, and roles array for downstream middleware
Token rotation invalidates the previous refresh token atomically within a transaction

userStories.title: Session management: concurrent session limits and device tracking
userStories.description: Extend the refresh token system to track active sessions per device/user-agent, enforce a maximum concurrent session limit (default 5), and provide an API for users to view and revoke their sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: refresh_tokens table includes device_name, ip_address, last_used_at columns
POST /api/auth/login records user_agent and IP in the refresh_token row
When a 6th session is created, the oldest unused session is automatically revoked (sliding window eviction)
GET /api/auth/sessions returns all active sessions for the current user with device info and last_used_at
DELETE /api/auth/sessions/:sessionId revokes a specific session (user can only revoke their own)
DELETE /api/auth/sessions revokes all sessions for the current user except the current one

userStories.title: Audit logging schema and service for auth events
userStories.description: Create a dedicated audit_log table and AuditService that records all authentication and authorization events. This provides a tamper-evident trail for security review.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates audit_log table with id, user_id, event_type, resource, resource_id, ip_address, user_agent, metadata JSONB, ts columns
AuditService.log(event) inserts a record and never throws — failures are swallowed with a warning log
audit_log table is append-only — no UPDATE or DELETE routes are exposed
event_type enum includes: login_success, login_failure, logout, token_refresh, oauth_link, role_assigned, role_revoked, permission_denied, password_changed
Index on user_id and ts for efficient per-user queries
GET /api/auth/audit-log returns paginated audit events, filterable by event_type and date range (requires settings:write)

userStories.title: Audit logging integration across all auth endpoints
userStories.description: Wire the AuditService into all authentication endpoints so that every login attempt, token operation, OAuth callback, and permission denial is recorded in the audit log with full context.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/login records login_success or login_failure with IP and user_agent
POST /api/auth/logout records logout event with the revoked session ID in metadata
POST /api/auth/refresh records token_refresh event
OAuth callback records oauth_link event when an identity is linked or created
requirePermission middleware records permission_denied event when access is refused (includes resource and action)
All audit log entries include the request IP address extracted from X-Forwarded-For or req.socket.remoteAddress

userStories.title: Password reset flow with secure token generation
userStories.description: Implement a complete password reset flow: request reset (email link), validate token, and set new password. Tokens are single-use, time-limited, and stored hashed in the database.
acceptanceCriteria: password_reset_tokens table stores hashed_token, user_id, expires_at (1 hour), used_at columns
POST /api/auth/forgot-password always returns 200 regardless of whether email exists (prevents enumeration)
Reset token is a cryptographically random 32-byte hex string hashed with SHA-256 before storage
POST /api/auth/reset-password validates token hash, checks expiry, marks used_at, and updates bcrypt password hash
Used or expired tokens return 400 ValidationError — not 401
Password reset records a password_changed audit log event and revokes all existing refresh tokens

userStories.title: RBAC UI panel in Settings for role and permission management
userStories.description: Add a Roles & Permissions tab to the Settings panel that allows admins to view roles, see their permissions, and manage user role assignments. Read-only for non-admin users.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings panel includes a new 'roles' tab visible to all users but editable only by admins
Roles list shows each role with its name, description, member count, and permission chips
Clicking a role opens a detail view listing all assigned permissions grouped by resource
Admin users can click a user row in the Members tab to open a role assignment modal
Role assignment modal shows current roles and allows adding/removing roles with immediate save
Non-admin users see the roles list as read-only with no edit controls

userStories.title: Auth system integration tests
userStories.description: Write Jest integration tests covering the critical paths of the RBAC, OAuth2, session, and audit logging systems. Tests run against a real test database instance.
acceptanceCriteria: Test: assignRoleToUser → hasPermission returns true for that resource/action
Test: requirePermission middleware returns 403 when user lacks permission, 200 when it has it
Test: POST /api/auth/refresh rotates tokens and invalidates old refresh token
Test: 6th concurrent session creation evicts the oldest session
Test: POST /api/auth/forgot-password + reset-password flow completes and old tokens are revoked
Test: login_failure and permission_denied events appear in audit_log after respective operations
